reason: The variance is real. WAGR-435 still says the VIP link-to-sign-up association is deferred to a future discovery session, and no Jira ticket records the 9/30 design. But the claim overstates 'users create the VIP link inside the flow' as the decision. Later in the same discussion (01:45:56), the direction changed: one default VIP link per deal (Owen adds it at deal creation), the flow finds it and ties it automatically, and creating the link in the flow is only the fallback when the deal has no VIP link. Kobi said this depends on there being 'only one VIP link'. Emily proposed it and Joyce did not explicitly confirm it.
q1: Found verbatim in the re-fetched Gemini notes for the 30 Sep 2026 11:30 EDT weekly sync (doc 1pc9pSc8tFg_8IuqTrOcRpNaRF9l8hiB6sjpqizzbqZo). Kobi's 'maybe we give them the ability to create it in this workflow as opposed to going to deals, finding the deal, adding the link,' is in the 01:43:51 block. Joyce's 'If you could make it automatically tagged as VIP as they're creating it.' / Kobi 'yes.' / Joyce 'Yeah, that makes sense.' is in the 01:44:56 block, with Kobi's 'and then creating it here.' and Joyce's 'will it attach to the deal?' / 'Oh, yeah... we would set it up that way' in between (the claim leaves these out, but they are consistent with it). The L3450 quote from Emily and Kobi was also found verbatim at 01:45:56.
q2: Partly supported. Context before the quote: at 01:42 Kobi and Emily first said VIP sign-ups need no link tracking. Joyce corrected this: she expected a link classified as VIP and attached to the deal, 'similar to our current flow'. Kobi then proposed creating the link in the sign-up flow, and Joyce agreed it should attach to the deal and be auto-tagged VIP. Context after the quote: Emily asked whether users must pick the link every time. Kobi said there is probably only one VIP link per deal. Emily proposed that Owen add the VIP link at deal creation as the default. Kobi responded 'If that's the case...': choose the deal, find the VIP link on that deal and tie it automatically, with a VIP tag on the link in addition to Exclude from CMS. The exception case is to raise an error or allow creating the link in the flow. So the meeting settled that the association is handled inside the VIP flow and is no longer deferred. The specific mechanism (auto-tie a default link vs create in the flow) is conditional and was not explicitly confirmed by the client. Kobi then closed the VIP topic ('I think those were the main things for VIP').
q3: No later meeting changes this. The ledger runs to 2026-09-30, and no rows exist after the cited meeting. The 9/30 rows L3449 (create in flow, decided) and L3450 (default VIP link at deal creation, proposed) are the latest. L3450 refines L3449 and does not reverse it.
q4: Not covered. WAGR-435 (Open, Unassigned, 1 comment) says the link-to-signup association was 'explicitly deferred to a future discovery session'. Its only comment (Kobi, 29 Sep) moves CMS exclusion to the generic WAGR-491 mechanism and does not mention association. WAGR-432 (Open, Unassigned, 0 comments, last updated 23 Sep) covers the sign-up's relation to the Deal but not the link. Epic WAGR-420 has no comments and was last updated 23 Sep. JQL 'project = WAGR AND text ~ "VIP"' returned WAGR-456, 435, 441, 197, 405, 160, 446, 432, 431, 434, 433, 420 and 412. None describes the 9/30 link design. WAGR-456 and WAGR-491 (both updated 2 Oct) say 'do not hard-code VIP semantics' and do not cover the VIP flow's link association. JQL for 'VIP link' updated since 30 Sep returned only WAGR-456, which does not cover it.
corrections: Restate the 9/30 outcome: link association is handled inside the VIP sign-up flow. Proposed mechanism: one default VIP link per deal (added at deal creation), found and tied automatically when the user picks the deal; if no VIP link exists, raise an error or let the user create it in the flow (auto-tagged VIP and attached to the deal). This depends on there being one VIP link per deal, which still needs confirmation from Joyce or Owen.
Speakers for the full evidence: Kobi Kunasekaran, Joyce Kiddell and Emily Vandenberg (Emily proposed the default-link approach).

The suggested action should target both WAGR-432 (sign-up flow and Deal relation) and WAGR-435 (remove the 'deferred to future discovery' constraint). It should also flag the open question of one VIP link per deal.
